html:
The idea, from the historian Fernand Braudel, that Russia before Peter the Great was a trading world of its own, mostly outside the European system centred on Amsterdam.

The Tsardom of Muscovy had the Volga River as its spine. Ivan the Terrible took Kazan in 1552 and Astrakhan in 1556, which opened the whole river down to the Caspian Sea and trade with Persia and Central Asia. In the north, Archangel on the White Sea, founded in 1584, was the one sea port to the west. English merchants of the Muscovy Company and later the Dutch came there for furs, hemp, tar and leather.

Eastward, the conquest of Siberia brought a flow of sable and other furs. Russia sold much and bought little, so Western silver came in and stayed.

For Braudel this made Muscovy a "world economy" with its own centre in Moscow, linked to Europe only at its edges. That changed after 1689, when Peter took power, opened the Baltic and built Saint Petersburg.
sum: The idea, from the historian Fernand Braudel, that Russia before Peter the Great was a trading world of its own, mostly outside the European system centred on Amsterdam.
